messages:
elaine: Hi - after upgrading to ts-sdk v2.3.1 our /rerank results are coming back in the wrong order. Scores appear to be compared lexicographically (e.g. 10 before 2). Also seeing some scores show up as null on the server side. Repro below.

elaine: Minimal repro: using node 18, ts-sdk@2.3.1, call: 
```ts
await client.rerank({
  model: 'rerank-001',
  input: 'query',
  candidates: ['a','b','c'],
  candidate_scores: [0, 1, 10]
});
```
Result: server returns ordering [c,b,a] (10,1,0). When I capture the raw request payload the scores are strings: "candidate_scores":["0","1","10"].

sam: Thanks — can you paste the raw request body you captured (network tab / proxy)? Also which exact ts-sdk package name/version?

elaine: Raw body (copied from Chrome devtools):
```json
{"model":"re-rank-001","input":"query","candidates":["a","b","c"],"candidate_scores":["0","1","10"]}
```
sdk version: `@redwood-inference/ts-sdk@2.3.1`

sam: that confirms it. Server expects numeric scores; if the SDK sends strings the server treats them as strings in the comparator -> lexicographic sort. The nulls you saw earlier are likely when a score was undefined and our serializer converted it to `null`.

jordan: I can reproduce locally. The bug is in the SDK serializer — we added a precision replacer in 2.3.0 to preserve decimals but it accidentally coerces all numbers to strings when applied broadly. Replacer code snippet (simplified):
```js
JSON.stringify(obj, (k,v) => typeof v === 'number' ? v.toFixed(6) : v)
```
That returns strings. We should return Number(parseFloat(...)) or avoid replacer on arrays meant to stay numeric.

support-bot: Ticket #INC-4821 created and escalated to eng. Assigned to @jordan.

elaine: Workaround I used: manually map candidate_scores: `candidate_scores: candidate_scores.map(Number)` before calling client.rerank. That fixed ordering for us.

jordan: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/infra/ts-sdk/pulls/235 — fix removes global number replacer, adds targeted formatting util, and adds test to ensure arrays of numbers are serialized as JSON numbers. Patch has tests for negative/zero/decimal/NaN cases.

sam: ETA for release? We have one customer on dedicated who hit this in prod.

jordan: Patch merged to main, cutting 2.3.2 release now. RC published to npm private registry: `@redwood-inference/ts-sdk@2.3.2-rc.1`. Final release ETA ~4 hours (manual QA + publish). We'll post here when live.

elaine: Great — I can validate once RC is public. Thanks for quick turnaround. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Update on INC-4821: status -> fix-deployed-to-canary.

jordan: Note: added guard to avoid turning `NaN` into string; server-side also now treats non-numeric candidates as error instead of silent null. We'll add a migration note in changelog.

sam: Please add a small snippet to the support KB about the workaround (map(Number)) and note affected versions 2.3.1 only.

elaine: Will do. Marking resolved for my case after RC verification.

jordan: Follow-up: if anyone sees weird localized numeric formatting (commas) in payloads capture raw body — that indicates similar replacer misuse.

elaine: Verified RC: `2.3.2-rc.1` fixed it for us. Closing thread.
